bites.title: Imports and project structure
bites.body: A module is a Python file you can import. import math brings in the math module. from pathlib import Path brings in one name. A package is a folder of modules you import as a group. Keep related files together so imports read like a path: from notes import parse. Circular imports, where two files import each other at the top, are a common generated-code tangle.

choices.text: A Python file you can import

questions.explanation: A module is a file of Python code. Importing it lets another file use its names.

questions.prompt: What does from pathlib import Path do?

choices.text: Makes the name Path available from that module

questions.explanation: pathlib is in the standard library. This import binds the name Path in your file.

bites.title: Reading library documentation
bites.body: When an assistant picks a library, read the docs for the version you have installed. Start with a short example, then the parameter list: what is required, what is optional, and what the function returns. Check the exceptions it raises. A blog post can be stale. The project's own docs, matched to your version, are the contract you are actually calling.
bites.sourceNote: Practice for reading library docs · confidence: high

questions.prompt: An assistant imports a library you do not know. What should you check first?

choices.text: The docs for the version you installed

questions.explanation: Behavior changes between versions. Match the docs to the version in your environment.

questions.prompt: Which question is most useful while reading a function's docs?

choices.text: What does it return, and what can it raise?
How many GitHub stars does it have?

questions.explanation: The return value and the errors tell you how to use the function and what can go wrong.
